title: MeanSquaredHolderNonconvex.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained differentiable objectives permitting nonconvexity, with globally L-Lipschitz gradient and f(x0) − inf f ≤ Δ. No minimizer attainment or convexity is required.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: One query (x,y) returns (g(x,ξ),g(y,ξ)) using the same sample. Samples are independent and identically distributed across calls. Each gradient estimate is unbiased. The budget counts paired queries, with a fixed upper limit including initialization and batches. All Params are public; f, g and the sampling law are hidden.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/MeanSquaredHolderNonconvex.lean: spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.admissible; LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: IID; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: The shared-sample oracle satisfies E‖g(x,ξ) − g(y,ξ)‖² ≤ M‖x−y‖^(2ν) globally, where M ≥ 0 and 1/2 ≤ ν ≤ 1. Separately, the objective gradient is globally L-Lipschitz with L > 0. Samplewise Lipschitz continuity is not assumed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniform finite variance E‖g(x,ξ) − ∇f(x)‖² ≤ σ², with σ ≥ 0. No exponential-tail or almost-sure noise bound is imposed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is a second-countable real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure; finite dimensionality is not required. Public parameters include L, M, ν, σ, Δ ≥ 0, ε > 0 and x0.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: Return a point X in E satisfying E‖∇f(X)‖ ≤ ε, using the unsquared norm. The output must be measurable and its gradient norm integrable; no particular iterate-selection rule is required.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The guarantee averages over both algorithm randomness and the IID oracle sequence, under their product probability law.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The formulation combines a Lipschitz objective gradient with a separately specified mean-square Hölder paired oracle, allowing ν < 1, in a potentially infinite-dimensional Hilbert space.

descriptionHtml:
Mean-Squared Hölder Nonconvex Optimization

We consider finding an approximate stationary point of a differentiable, possibly nonconvex function f:E→R on a separable real Hilbert space E. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz, where L>0, and a given point x0∈E satisfies f(x0)−infx∈Ef(x)≤Δ, where Δ≥0. At a pair x,y∈E, the oracle returns unbiased gradient estimates g(x,ξ),g(y,ξ) using one shared sample ξ, with independent samples across calls. Their variance is bounded by σ2, and their mean-squared difference by M∥x−y∥2ν, where σ,M≥0 and ν∈[1/2,1]. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈E with E∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε, averaging over oracle and independent algorithm randomness.

The underlying optimization problem is infx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E. The algorithm receives E, the measurable sample space Ω, x0, and all parameters L,M,ν,σ,Δ,ε.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Smoothness and initial gap). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E. For every x,y∈E, ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,f(x0)−f(x)≤Δ.

Assumption 2 (Unbiased stochastic gradients). There exist a probability measure p on Ω and a jointly measurable map g:E×Ω→E. For every x∈E, the random vector g(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable and ∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2 is integrable under ξ∼p, with Eξ∼p[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼p[∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2]≤σ2.

Assumption 3 (Mean-squared Hölder continuity). For every x,y∈E, the random variable ∥g(x,ξ)−g(y,ξ)∥2 is integrable under ξ∼p, and Eξ∼p[∥g(x,ξ)−g(y,ξ)∥2]≤M∥x−y∥2ν.

At call k≥0, a query (xk,yk)∈E×E receives the pair (g(xk,ξk),g(yk,ξk)). The measurable samples (ξk)k≥0 are mutually independent with common law p, and are independent of the algorithm’s randomness. Both evaluations within a pair use the same sample; one returned pair counts as one oracle call. Queries may depend on preceding replies.

After the allotted calls, the output x¯ must be measurable, its gradient norm must be integrable, and it must satisfy EP[∥∇f(x¯)∥]≤ε, where P is the joint law of the oracle samples and the algorithm’s randomness.

comparisonHtml:
On a second-countable real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure, f is differentiable, ∇f is L-Lipschitz, and f(x0)−inff≤Δ. Here L,ε>0, M,σ,Δ≥0, and ν∈[1/2,1]. The jointly measurable oracle g uses IID samples of law p, is unbiased, and satisfies Ep∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2≤σ2 and Ep∥g(x,ξ)−g(y,ξ)∥2≤M∥x−y∥2ν, with the stated moments integrable. A pair query evaluates two points using the same sample. The target is a measurable output with ∫∥∇f(xout(ω))∥dP(ω)≤ε, where P is the execution law. Comparisons to cited prior-work statements use E=Rd.

import LongTails.Template
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.MeanSquaredHolderNonconvex

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  [countableE : SecondCountableTopology E]
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L : ℝ
  M : ℝ
  ν : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.innerE Params.completeE Params.measurableE
  Params.borelE Params.countableE Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E × p.E
  Reply p := p.E × p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.M ∧ 1 / 2 ≤ q.ν ∧ q.ν ≤ 1 ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 0 ≤ q.Δ ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (g : q.E → q.Ω → q.E) (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω)),
      LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
        (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k) (p : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
      O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
            law := P
            answer := fun _ (_, z) ω => (g z.1 ω, g z.2 ω) } ∧
      (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
      (∀ x y, ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
      (∀ x, f q.x0 - f x ≤ q.Δ) ∧
      Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
      (∀ x, Integrable (g x) p) ∧
      (∀ x, ∫ ω, g x ω ∂p = gradient f x) ∧
      (∀ x, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 2) p) ∧
      (∀ x, ∫ ω, ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 2 ∂p ≤ q.σ ^ 2) ∧
      (∀ x y, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g x ω - g y ω‖ ^ 2) p) ∧
      (∀ x y, ∫ ω, ‖g x ω - g y ω‖ ^ 2 ∂p ≤ q.M * ‖x - y‖ ^ (2 * q.ν))
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => ‖gradient f (output ω)‖) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∫ ω, ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.MeanSquaredHolderNonconvex
